why: The student gives none of the three update statements (count = count + 1; count += 1; count++;). The one correct point is that printing count + 1 or just evaluating it does not store the result back into count, so this covers one part of the increment and stops there.

concepts.quote: count + 1 on its own line does not change count
concepts.why: It sees that the increment has to store the result back into count, but it never writes a statement that does this.
Right: the call evaluates count + 1 and prints it, and no variable changes.

concepts.quote: shows one more, but ... does not change count
concepts.why: Right: writing to output adds text but does not change count.

concepts.quote: count + 1 on its own line does not change count
concepts.why: The answer treats count + 1; as a statement that runs and does nothing, but Java rejects it at compile time with 'not a statement', because a plain addition is not a valid expression statement.
